title: Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)
text:
Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset) - Overview
# Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)

Binary sentiment classification (positive / negative) of Arabic hotel reviews,
using the HARD balanced dataset (Elnagar, Khalifa & Einea, 2018).

title: Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)
text:
Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset) - Source and license
- Data: https://github.com/elnagara/HARD-Arabic-Dataset (`data/balanced-reviews.zip`),
  collected from Booking.com in June/July 2016. Modern Standard + dialectal Arabic.
- The source repository ships **no explicit LICENSE file**; the authors distribute it for
  research use with a citation request. This project is educational portfolio work
  and cites: Elnagar A., Khalifa Y.S., Einea A. (2018), Hotel Arabic-Reviews Dataset
  Construction for Sentiment Analysis Applications, Springer SCI vol 740, pp 35-52,
  doi:10.1007/978-3-319-67056-0_3.
- Raw reviews are not redistributed; the dataset is downloaded from the public
  source repository above by the project's fetch script.

title: Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)
section: Evaluation protocol (frozen 2026-11-04 before any model fitting)
text:
Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset) - Evaluation protocol (frozen 2026-11-04 before any model fitting)
1. Labels: rating 1-2 -> negative (0), rating 4-5 -> positive (1). Ratings of 3 do
   not occur in this balanced subset.
2. Light normalization only: remove Arabic diacritics and tatweel, unify alef
   variants and yaa forms. No stemming, no external lexicons.
3. Split: **group split by hotel** (GroupShuffleSplit, test 20%, seed 42) - no hotel
   appears in both train and test, so the evaluation measures generalization to
   hotels the model never saw, not memorized property-specific wording.
4. The TF-IDF vectorizer is fit on the training reviews only.
5. Models compared on the untouched test set exactly once: majority-class dummy,
   MultinomialNB, and logistic regression. No post-hoc tuning after viewing test
   results. All metrics reported as-is, including any baseline we fail to beat.
6. Limitations stated plainly: reviews are from 2016 Booking.com hotels; the label
   is derived from star ratings; single frozen split, no cross-validation claim.

title: Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)
text:
Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset) - CURRENT RESULTS (2026-11-05)
A fresh full training run on 22,396 reviews after removing duplicates reached 94.6% accuracy, F1 0.948 and AUC 0.983, with 5 tests passing. The number is measured on the same test set used during development (benchmark reuse, not a new independent confirmation).

title: Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset)
text:
Arabic Hotel Review Sentiment (HARD dataset) - Layout
- `src/prepare.py` - load, normalize, label, group-split; writes data/train.pkl, data/test.pkl
- `src/train.py` - fit vectorizer + models, evaluate once, write metrics.json + model.joblib
- `src/app.py` - FastAPI serving the saved pipeline (Arabic input)
- `tests/` - pytest suite (split integrity, label mapping, train-only fitting, prediction sanity, API)

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - Overview
# BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval

DSAI201 coursework from the archive of Ahmed Khalifa: an inverted index over BBC
text news (2,225 articles), plus a separate AI-assisted post-coursework
improvement that adds TF-IDF and then a hybrid semantic ranker as explicit
extensions. Personal contribution to the original coursework is unconfirmed; no
unaided-authorship or submission claim is made.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - What actually ran
Original cells 3 and 4 only, using the current downloaded public data path: cell 4 fails
with NameError (preprocess not defined) because the original calls the function before
a later cell defines it. No full original or repaired-original run is claimed. The native
original had 10 historical outputs; the portfolio copy strips them to avoid
redistributing source excerpts.
The improved final source executed on all 2,225 articles twice; postings and run report
byte-identical across reruns. 10 tests passed. CLI query also executed.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - What actually ran
Downloaded source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/pariza/bbc-news-summary/data
Kagglehub handle pariza/bbc-news-summary, version 2, downloaded 2026-11-04.
Rights reference: http://mlg.ucd.ie/datasets/bbc.html . UCD states non-commercial
and research use only; BBC owns original article copyright. Kaggle CC0 metadata
conflicts with these terms and is NOT treated as permission to redistribute.
No raw articles/summaries, index/postings, trained TF-IDF state or copied excerpts
are redistributed in this archive. Runtime artifacts stay local.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - CURRENT IMPROVED VERSION (2026-11-05)
The improved search is a hybrid of TF-IDF and semantic embeddings, evaluated before/after under a frozen protocol: the known article is the first result for 135 of 150 queries, and topical-relevance precision at the first 5 results rose from 0.68 to 0.80. On the held-out sample, known-article lookup did not improve (128 versus 131 for the baseline), so the real gain is topical relevance. The relevance judgments are the authors' own, not an independent benchmark, and the topical-relevance stage had no held-out check.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - Substantive improvements
- Correct run order in separate standalone module; original retained unchanged.
- Article-only root discovery, excludes summaries. Download includes 8,900 TXT files
  due to TWO duplicate trees, each 2,225 articles + 2,225 summaries. Compare relative
  paths + SHA256 for every article in roots, fail if they disagree, select one.
- Deterministic category/filename IDs; file basenames alone collide across topics.
- All 2,225 articles used, no traversal-first-350 selection or category-label reranking.
- 2,127 unique content hashes: 98 exact-content duplicates beyond first occurrences,
  retained as distinct source IDs and reported. Search hits may repeat content;
  they are not independent evidence. No claim of a deduplicated corpus.
- Explicit encoding: 2,224 UTF8, 1 cp1252, errors do not silently yield empty text.
- Inverted postings frequencies, deterministic order and tie-breaking.
- Two selectable rankers. Search(rows) defaults to hybrid: 0.65 * TF-IDF cosine
  + 0.35 * MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding cosine (adopted 2026-11-04, eval/EXPERIMENTS.md)
  - intended for topical queries (best judged relevance). Search(rows,
  mode='tfidf') keeps the original sparse baseline runnable - intended for exact
  known-item lookup (slightly better held-out strict findability, no model
  download). Empty/OOV queries yield no hits in both modes. Hybrid first run
  downloads the ~90 MB model from Hugging Face (cached afterwards); indexing
  encodes the corpus once (~100 s CPU).
- Manifest hashes/counters, source provenance, invalid-root guards and tests.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - Results and retrieval evaluation
Categories: business 510 / entertainment 386 / politics 417 / sport 511 / tech 401.
Inverted vocabulary 27,906; TF-IDF 2,225 x 27,609 after English stopword removal.
Retrieval quality is measured in eval/RESULTS.md (added 2026-11-04): known-item
top-5 150/150 (MRR 0.954), judged topical queries P@5 0.80 / P@10 0.70, both
development-set numbers with an honest held-out known-item check reported.
Judgments are author-built (two judges, originals preserved) and shipped for
re-checking, not an independent benchmark; no personal-skill claim.
Article-derived query IDs/scores in run_report.json are diagnostics, not a scorecard.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - Reproduce
Python 3.10 verified. sentence-transformers 6.2.0 + torch 2.14.1+cpu added for the
hybrid ranker (CPU-only, no GPU needed). requirements.lock.txt is the exact tested environment (includes
some unrelated prior verification dependencies, conservative not minimal).
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.venv/bin/python test_news_index.py
.venv/bin/python news_index.py --download --output local-output
.venv/bin/python news_index.py --download --query "football world cup"
Or give local dataset root as positional argument instead of --download.
No Kaggle account/auth or paid API used. Local output may contain copyrighted terms;
do not redistribute generated postings, data or article text without clearance.

title: BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval
text:
BBC News Article Indexing and Retrieval - Tests
Unique category IDs; summary exclusion; agreeing roots not doubled; disagreeing
roots rejected; missing article root; term counts; duplicate IDs rejected; known
synthetic search; deterministic manifest/index; deterministic tie order. Tests use
invented tiny text fixtures only. Whole-data execution is separate from unit tests.
Source/output/config secret scan completed before packaging, no literals flagged.

title: CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1)
text:
CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1) - Overview
# CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1)

University coursework from the archive of Ahmed Khalifa. Four models
trained and compared on CIFAR-10: a baseline CNN, a manually built ResNet, a manually
built Inception-style network, and VGG16 transfer learning.

Author: Ahmed Khalifa, DSAI308 Deep Learning course project.
Packaged from the preserved original submission with AI-assistant help.
Team status: not recorded; no team or solo claim is made.

title: CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1)
section: CURRENT RESULTS: official-split retrain (updated 2026-11-06, current headline)
text:
CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1) - CURRENT RESULTS: official-split retrain (updated 2026-11-06, current headline)
The four models were retrained from scratch on the official CIFAR-10 split: 50,000 official training images (with a separate 5,000-image validation set) and the official 10,000-image test set. The protocol was locked before the test numbers were seen and no model was selected on test results. Current best: the manual ResNet reaches **89.51% test accuracy / 0.8947 macro-F1**, validation-selected from a 4-epoch continuation of the 20-epoch model with full optimizer state carried (benchmark reuse on the development-exposed official test set). The other official-test accuracies: VGG16 transfer learning 86.01%, baseline CNN 77.66%, manual Inception 67.24%. An earlier model trained partly on corrupted data was excluded and retrained cleanly. Two of the four models stay below 80%.

title: CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1)
section: CURRENT RESULTS: official-split retrain (updated 2026-11-06, current headline)
text:
CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1) - CURRENT RESULTS: official-split retrain (updated 2026-11-06, current headline)
Superseded headline (kept for provenance): an earlier 2026-11-06 warm-start epoch-1 candidate scored 88.48% (20-epoch baseline: 87.55%); the CNN 77.66% is the validation-selected checkpoint after restoring the frozen selection protocol (last-epoch weights: 75.03%); the Inception 67.24% is a warm start bounded by a 600-second fit cap (last-epoch: 65.42%). VGG16 was not refit.

CIFAR-10 Deep Learning (DSAI308 Assignment 1) - HISTORICAL results: custom split, reloaded saved models (2026-11-04; superseded as the headline by the official-split retrain and its 2026-11-06 updates)

| 2 | ResNet (manual blocks) | 0.8520 |

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Overview
# Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning

End-to-end machine learning project: a classifier that estimates the
probability that a food commodity's average monthly price in Egypt will
rise more than 2% in the next month, trained on WFP food price data and
served through a FastAPI web app.

![App screenshot](figures/app_screenshot.png)

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Why this task
A first attempt at plain next-month price *regression* on this data found
that a persistence baseline ("next month = this month") is essentially
impossible to beat - Egyptian monthly food prices are smooth with step
jumps. Rather than ship a model that loses to its baseline, the project
reframes the problem as the question machine learning actually answers
better here: **is a price jump coming?** The classifier beats both the
majority-class and previous-month baselines on a strict time holdout.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Results
**Protocol.** Chronological windows with every fitting date strictly before
every served date: train < Oct 2024, isotonic calibration on Oct 2024 -
Sep 2025, retrospective evaluation on Oct 2025 - Sep 2026. The pipeline
(model, features, 2% spike definition, 0.5 threshold) was frozen before the
evaluation run. This is a retrospective development evaluation: the window
was reproduced and reused across versions, so it is not an untouched
one-shot final test.

**Retrospective evaluation (Oct 2025 - Sep 2026, 215 series-months):**

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Results
| Metric | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| ROC AUC | **0.759** (all 215) | 0.500 (random). Paired on the 192 series-months with a prior month: model 0.750 vs 0.625 (previous month spiked) |
| Brier (raw / calibrated) | 0.141 / **0.138** | - |
| Accuracy (raw threshold 0.5) | 0.795 | 0.800 (majority) / 0.805 (previous month spiked) |
| Accuracy (calibrated threshold 0.5) | 0.800 | same baselines |
| F1 (spike class, raw threshold 0.5) | 0.353 | - |

Reading: the model carries real ranking signal - paired on the 192 scored
months with a prior month, model AUC 0.750 vs 0.625 for a prev-month-spike
rule - and calibration measurably improves its scores. At a 0.5 threshold its accuracy does NOT
beat trivial baselines on this window - reported as-is; the app presents a
calibrated risk score with baselines shown, not an accuracy claim.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Results
**v4 model change (2026-11-04).** The classifier is now
HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=200, learning_rate=0.03,
l2_regularization=1.0, max_leaf_nodes=15), replacing the v3
(max_iter=600) model. The variant was selected on rolling origins
2016-2022 ONLY (mean AUC .637 -> .664, min AUC .511 -> .529, mean
calibrated Brier .2391 -> .2218); the 2024-10 origin above was excluded
from selection. All origins are development-exposed data, not a holdout.
v4 leads v3 on 3 of 4 selection origins and trails on 2016; on no origin
does it beat the previous-month heuristic on accuracy. Full tables,
protocol freeze and negative findings: `ROBUSTNESS.md`,
`PROTOCOL_FREEZE.md`, `rolling_origin_eval.json`, `baseline_compare.json`.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Results
**Honesty boundary.** The entire dataset was exposed during development
(task framing, model class, features and hyperparameters were chosen after
exploratory scoring of several windows). These numbers are a RETROSPECTIVE
evaluation of a frozen pipeline - there is no independent final test on
this dataset, and none is claimed. Full numbers and the protocol in
`models/metrics.json`; curves in `figures/roc_pr_curves.png` and
`figures/calibration_curve.png`.

**Late-issued October 2026 ledger.** A month-ahead spike-risk ledger for
October 2026 was frozen on 2026-11-05 - issued late, after the month it
covers, so it is a backfill (late-issued) evaluation ledger, not a
prospective forecast - and will be scored when WFP publishes October
actuals. The frozen scoring rule is in `prospective/score_ledger.py`.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - How leakage is prevented
- Features for a target month use only observations strictly before it.
- Lags are calendar-exact: `price_lag_k` is the price exactly k months
  earlier and `NaN` when that month was not observed (the Cairo series has
  gaps) - never a row-shift that smuggles future information across a gap.
- Chronological windows (train < 2024-10, calibrate 2024-10..2025-09,
  evaluate >= 2025-10), identical cutoffs for every series.
- The calibrator is fit only on the calibration window, on a model trained
  only on the training window - no future-to-past calibration.
- As-of serving rule: the app refuses to score months inside the training
  or calibration windows (before 2025-10) because those scores would be
  in-sample; every served score has all fit/calibration dates strictly
  before the scored month (asserted by tests).
- `tests/test_features.py` proves the no-leakage property: changing a
  month's price leaves that same month's features unchanged.
- `tests/test_split.py` proves the chronological windows are disjoint and
  global, that the artifact's train/calibration max dates strictly precede
  every servable date, that app prediction rows align with the exact
  preceding calendar months' real prices, and that in-sample history
  checks are refused.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Project structure
```
src/features.py   calendar-exact lag + derived feature pipeline
src/train.py      trains HistGradientBoostingClassifier, writes model + metrics
src/evaluate.py   regenerates ROC/PR curves and holdout example plot
src/app.py        FastAPI app: web UI + JSON API
templates/        single-page UI
tests/            25 tests: leakage, artifact, API contract
data/             WFP/HDX source CSV (see data/DATA_SOURCE.md)
models/           model.joblib, metrics.json, holdout_predictions.csv
figures/          evaluation curves + app screenshot
```

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Run it
```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python src/train.py        # reproduces models/ artifacts
python src/evaluate.py     # reproduces figures/
pytest tests/ -q           # 25 tests
uvicorn app:app --app-dir src --port 8000
# open http://localhost:8000
```

The API: `GET /api/series` lists the 47 series with evaluation metrics;
`POST /api/predict` returns the calibrated spike-risk score for the month
after the series' last observation (Oct 2026), with the model's training
and calibration date cutoffs attached - a retrospective as-of demo, not a
live forecast or verified probability; `POST /api/history-check` scores
the most recent scoreable month (>= Oct 2025, refusing in-sample months)
as-of the previous one and shows the actual outcome.
The UI supports deep links, e.g.
`/?market=Cairo%20(national%20average)&commodity=Rice&auto=1`.

title: Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning
text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - Honest limitations
- This is a screening signal, not a price forecast: it estimates jump
  risk, not the future price level.
- Only two price series exist in the source data (national averages);
  the model does not predict governorate-level prices.
- Macro shocks (currency devaluations) drive many spikes and are only
  indirectly visible through price momentum features.

text:
Egypt Food Price Spike Early Warning - License
Code: MIT (see LICENSE). Data: WFP via HDX, CC BY-IGO - see
data/DATA_SOURCE.md for attribution.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Overview
# Image-caption BM25 search

A DSAI201 image-caption search implementation from the coursework archive of
Ahmed Khalifa, plus a separate AI-assisted post-coursework improvement. Ahmed's
personal contribution is unconfirmed (original coursework); no unaided
authorship or university-submission claim is made. Not computer vision:
search ranks caption TEXT, not image pixels. No external images fetched or verified.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Provenance
Originals (34-cell notebook, 2-page report) are preserved privately and not
redistributed. The separate BBC Phase 1 is another source, NOT this project's
implementation.
Current public data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/220k-gpt4vision-image-captions
Upstream: https://huggingface.co/datasets/laion/220k-GPT4Vision-captions-from-LIVIS
Upstream card: captions are Mistral-7B-OpenOrca summaries of LVIS-Instruct4V
dialogues, not a claim all final captions were directly written by GPT4Vision.
Kaggle reports CC0; upstream metadata Apache 2.0. External COCO image rights remain
separate. No raw captions/URLs, dataset, generated index or model state is
redistributed. Included screenshots use invented synthetic captions only.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Actual execution and limits
Original CORE cells 1,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,13,16,17,18,19,23,24,25,27,28,29,33 executed
on current downloaded v2 data, changing only the local data path. 217,868 rows / 21,277 terms /
8,078,942 tokens, 88.8 seconds in the build environment. Gradio launch, download cell and pickle
save/load omitted. This is NOT a full original run or proof of historical-file identity.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Actual execution and limits
Final improved source whole-corpus runs repeat the same acceptance, matrix, result IDs
and scores except timings. 217,868 input; 0 invalid/blank captions or URLs; 1 exact
caption+URL duplicate removed; 217,867 accepted. BM25 217,867 x 277,468 stemmed unigram+bigram features.
Source CSV SHA256 d23256511d8ca679e8dd34b2df94e8186a8acb93b0bb6163055a5e6adf5d617e .
Retrieval quality is measured in eval/RESULTS.md with a frozen before/after
protocol. Current ranker (BM25+bigram): known-item full-caption lookup 150/150,
realistic partial-word recall top-1 140/150, top-5 150/150 (MRR 0.963), judged
topical queries P@1 0.9 / P@6 0.800 with named failure modes. Before this change
(TF-IDF cosine): partial-word top-1 67/150, top-5 101/150 (MRR 0.547), judged
P@1 1.0 / P@6 0.767. Judgments are author-built and shipped for re-checking, not
an independent benchmark; the new pool was re-judged under
the same rubric. Scores are BM25 scores, NOT probabilities; expansion remains
unbenchmarked. No speed-superiority claim. Current corpus build takes about 8 seconds on
the reference machine only; not comparable to the original core time, which includes
different steps. No paid APIs.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Changes in separate improved version
- Explicit CSV path/schema checks, no nondeterministic last-CSV selection.
- Missing captions rejected rather than turning NaN into literal text; URL validation;
  sequential reject-union then exact-pair dedup, stable original row IDs.
- Cached consistent stemming across corpus, query and OPTIONAL manual expansion.
  Expansion integrated into the UI, off by default, unbenchmarked and may reduce relevance.
- Sublinear TF / smoothed IDF / L2-normalized cosine replaced the original raw TF*log(N/(df+1)).
- BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75, Robertson DF smoothing) over stemmed unigram+bigram features
  then replaced TF-IDF cosine after measured comparison on the frozen eval
  protocol: partial known-item top-1 67->140/150, top-5 101->150, MRR
  0.547->0.963; judged topical P@1 1.0->0.9, mean P@6 0.767->0.800 (comparable).
  Details, candidate-variant comparison, and an untouched held-out
  confirmation (disjoint 150-caption sample: TF-IDF 69/105/0.553 vs BM25+bigram
  137/146/0.939 top-1/top-5/MRR) in eval/RESULTS.md. The development 150-sample
  and 10 judged queries were used for variant selection and are labeled
  development-only. Original TF-IDF pool and judgments preserved at
  eval/judged_pool_tfidf.json / eval/judgments_tfidf.json; the new pool was
  re-judged under the same rubric (see RESULTS.md).
- Auto-escaped template, restricted HTTP(S) link scheme, no credentials in URL,
  noreferrer/noopener links, CSP prevents automatic remote images/scripts.
- HTTP source links remain labeled HTTP, NOT silently rewritten to HTTPS. Links may
  be stale/inappropriate; opening a link visits an outside site. No automatic fetch.
- Empty/OOV state, 500-character query limit, deterministic ties, no pickle loading.
  Rebuilds the sparse index from CSV on startup; no persisted trusted-model claim.

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Reproduce
Python 3.10 verified; requirements.lock.txt is the exact tested environment but includes unrelated prior
verification dependencies, not a minimal specification.
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.venv/bin/python test_search.py
.venv/bin/python download_data.py
Use the returned exact train.csv path:
.venv/bin/python image_search.py /path/to/train.csv --output local-output --serve
Open http://127.0.0.1:8052 . Local-only, no deployment/tunnel.
Synthetic demonstration without the dataset:
.venv/bin/python image_search.py synthetic_fixture.csv --output demo-output --serve --demo

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Verified tests and pixels
11 unit tests: ranking, empty, OOV, integrated expansion, matching stems, bad URL,
HTML escape/CSP, missing-caption/duplicate accounting, missing column, query limit,
stable ties. Actual browser: synthetic search/empty/expansion and a full-corpus query

title: Image-caption BM25 search
text:
Image-caption BM25 search - Verified tests and pixels
Intermediate fix: a first strict HTTPS-only data run accepted 0 because source URLs use
HTTP. Allowed labeled HTTP(S), no rewriting, reran the final source and tests. A UI fixture
run overwrote a local diagnostic output folder; corrected by rerunning the full corpus
into a distinct final-full-output and comparing rerun results. The delivered aggregate
report comes only from the final full-corpus run. No silent mixing of fixture metrics.

Secret-pattern scan and source/output/config review done before packaging.
Raw baseline logs containing source caption excerpts intentionally NOT included.

title: Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project)
text:
Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project) - Overview
# Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project)

University coursework from the archive of Ahmed Khalifa. A neural
network implemented twice and compared: once from scratch in pure NumPy (forward
propagation, backpropagation, softmax cross-entropy, gradient descent all written
by hand) and once with Keras, on two datasets (Iris and MNIST).

Author: Ahmed Khalifa, DSAI253 Machine Learning.
Packaged from the preserved original notebook with AI-assistant help.
Team status: not recorded; no team or solo claim is made.

title: Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project)
section: Verified results (re-run end-to-end on Google Colab, 2026-11-04)
text:
Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project) - Verified results (re-run end-to-end on Google Colab, 2026-11-04)
| Dataset | Model | Accuracy | Final loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iris (2-class subset) | From scratch (NumPy) | 1.0000 | 0.0032 |
| Iris | Keras | 1.0000 | 0.1143 |
| MNIST (19,700 train / 5,700 test subset) | From scratch (NumPy) | 0.9584 | 0.0122 |
| MNIST (same subset) | Keras | 0.9326 | 0.2249 |

Note: the notebook deliberately uses a reduced MNIST subset (19,700 train / 5,700
test images), not the full 60k/10k split, so these numbers are not comparable to
published full-MNIST benchmarks. Iris is used as a binary (classes 0 and 1) task
for the scratch model.

title: Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project)
text:
Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project) - CURRENT ADDENDA (2026-11-05)
A re-run of the same notebook procedure scored 96.51% on the full official 10,000-image MNIST test set (95.84% on the first 5,700 test images, 97.395% on the remaining tail). The original exposure of the other test images during development is not documented, so this is not an independent confirmation, and the package ships no saved original weights. A matched ten-seed comparison on the same split and the 10,000-image test set gave 96.26% (sd 0.11) for the from-scratch NumPy network and 96.25% (sd 0.11) for Keras with the matched setup. Keras with an Adam recipe gave 94.78%. The gradient check covers tiny random networks only.

title: Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project)
section: Fix applied during packaging (documented, not hidden)
text:
Neural Network From Scratch vs Keras (DSAI253 Machine Learning project) - Fix applied during packaging (documented, not hidden)
The preserved original notebook crashed at the MNIST section with
`NameError: name 'y_train_onehot' is not defined` - the one-hot encoding step was
missing. One line was added in front of that cell, marked with a code comment:

    y_train_onehot = np.eye(10)[y_train_mnist]

Nothing else was changed; every other cell is byte-identical to the original.
The archived verification log records the full before/after evidence.

# Movies data validation

DSAI202 coursework (Assignment 1) from the archive of Ahmed Khalifa, with an
AI-assisted post-coursework validation script. Ahmed's exact personal
contribution to the original assignment is unconfirmed. The original assignment
carried course instructions prohibiting AI-generated submission work; this

title: Movies data validation
text:
Movies data validation - Verification scope
Tested 2026-11-04 on Python 3.10. Public mirror input: 9,999 rows, 9 columns.
Mirror: https://joannabieri.com/mathdatascience/data/movies.csv
Candidate dataset source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/bharatnatrayn/movies-dataset-for-feature-extracion-prediction
The mirror matches the saved notebook's schema, shape and first records, but is NOT
byte-verified against the original coursework CSV. Findings are for this
mirror. Dataset rights were not established; no CSV, row-level outputs or full
profiling HTML is redistributed here. The generated profile was visually inspected.

title: Movies data validation
text:
Movies data validation - Conservative portfolio default
- Parse start year while retaining YEAR_RAW unchanged and missing years as missing.
- Use actual Cerberus validators and exact genre tokens; GX suite/checkpoint execute.
- Preserve all statistical extremes, flagged by IQR_FLAG, not removed as erroneous.
- No median imputation or scaling in default output. Raw snapshot preserved at runtime.
- Explicitly separate 80 missing-genre exclusions and 429 exact duplicates removed;
  sequential disjoint accounting: 9,999-80-429=9,490 default rows.
- Default keeps 579 missing years. 1,991 IQR-flagged rows stay in the default output.
- Optional --pedagogical branch mirrors coursework-style median imputation/scaling
  and IQR exclusion, explicitly labeled PEDAGOGICAL. It excludes 2,523 rows AFTER
  imputation, leaving 6,967. Different IQR counts arise because imputation changes
  quartiles; neither is a claim that extremes are errors. Missing years imputed in
  this branch are NOT recovered historical facts. YEAR_RAW remains unchanged.
- Inferred pandera schema describes observed types, not business validity.

title: Movies data validation
text:
Movies data validation - Run
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.venv/bin/python portfolio_movies.py /path/to/movies.csv --output outputs --profile
.venv/bin/python test_movies.py

Tests expect the verified-output folder from the reported run; for a fresh run use
--output verified-output. Test counts 136 and 9,999-row conservation are fixture-specific.
The profile is minimal=True, not the original full profiling configuration.
No learned models or predictive results are claimed. Original install/profiling cells
were excluded from the baseline reproduction; all other original code ran. Improved
script INCLUDING profiling ran successfully; 4 regression tests passed.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - Overview
# Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)

A compact convolutional neural network trained **from scratch** to classify
real-world German traffic signs into 43 classes, evaluated on the
**GTSRB test set (12,630 images; decoded pixel and label identity with the
official test set was verified on 2026-11-05, see CURRENT STATUS)** plus the mirror's motion-blur corruption variant.
Includes a small FastAPI demo app and a pytest suite.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
section: CURRENT STATUS (2026-11-05, supersedes the mirror caveats below where they differ)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - CURRENT STATUS (2026-11-05, supersedes the mirror caveats below where they differ)
The official GTSRB archives were obtained (via the Wayback Machine, with independently pinned hashes) and the 12,630-image test set and 26,640-image training subset were decoded and checked: pixel and label identity with the mirror is verified. The shipped prepare script and model reproduce 98.8915% accuracy on the verified official test set (98.89%), with images resized to 32x32 and training on a 26,640-image subset of the official 39,209 training images. There are 0 exact duplicates between the original and the 32x32 images. The earlier one-duplicate audit result was not reproduced. Motion-blur provenance is still not officially verified. Training used a subset (26,640 of the official 39,209 training images), not the full set.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
section: Results (actual executed run, 4 Nov 2026; historical wording follows)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - Results (actual executed run, 4 Nov 2026; historical wording follows)
- 24 training epochs, ~10 min total on 2 CPU cores (no GPU, no paid compute).
- Saved-model reload verified deterministic (identical predictions).
- Model selection: fixed 24-epoch schedule chosen before any test use; final
  epoch kept (no best-checkpoint selection, no early stopping); the official-size
  test split was evaluated exactly once, after training. Percentages shown by the
  demo app are softmax confidence scores, not calibrated correctness
  probabilities.
- Weakest classes reported in `metrics.json` (e.g. "snow/ice warning" 82.0%,
  "empty red circle" 91.9%) - see `confusion_matrix.png` and `misclassified.png`.
- 6/6 pytest tests pass: class map, forward shape, reload determinism,
  metrics sanity, live app endpoints incl. bad-input handling, real-image sanity.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - Data provenance and honest limits
- Source: GTSRB benchmark (Stallkamp et al., 2012). The original host
  (benchmark.ini.rub.de) was unreachable from the build environment on
  2026-11-04, so the Hugging Face mirror `tanganke/gtsrb` was used.
  Downloaded files were verified by SHA-256 against the mirror's
  content-addressed metadata (all matched); the test split has the official
  12,630-image count. HISTORICAL (2026-11-04, superseded by the CURRENT STATUS
  above): at that time mirror-vs-original byte identity was not claimed.
- The mirror's train split is a 26,640-image subset of the official 39,209-image
  training set; training used 90% of it (23,976) with 2,664 for validation.
  This is disclosed, not the full official training set. HISTORICAL (2026-11-04,
  superseded): the mirror documents no split derivation, so the test split was then
  reported only as "same count as the official GTSRB test set". The CURRENT STATUS
  supersedes this: the test split was later verified identical to the official one
  (decoded pixels and labels). The byte-level identity of the mirror's files was never
  claimed; official-test identity was.
- Overlap audit (per-image SHA-1): internal validation vs test = 0 exact
  duplicates. HISTORICAL (2026-11-04 audit, not
  reproduced on 2026-11-05 - see CURRENT STATUS): mirror-train vs test showed
  exactly 1 duplicate image (test index 0, class "20 kph speed limit");
  accuracy excluding it was then unchanged at 98.89% (98.8914% vs 98.8915%).
- The motion_blur split is the mirror's precomputed corruption of the same
  12,630 test images (labels identical, per-index image correlation 0.95-0.99);
  exact official corruption provenance is not proven.
- Images were resized to 32x32. Class names come from the mirror's dataset card.
- The motion-blur variant is the mirror's precomputed corruption of the same
  test images (GTSRB-C style), used for robustness evaluation only.
- **No dataset images are redistributed in this package** (`data/` is git-ignored
  and excluded). GTSRB usage rights remain with its original publishers;
  this package is code, metrics, and a trained model for portfolio review.
- This is recognition of cropped sign images, not detection in full road scenes,
  and not a safety-critical system.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - Layout
- `src/model.py` - CompactCNN (~0.67M parameters, 32x32x3 input).
- `src/train.py` - time-budgeted, checkpoint-resumable training
  (random affine augmentation: rotation +/-10 deg, translation +/-10%, scale 0.9-1.1;
  SGD+nesterov, cosine LR, weight decay 5e-4).
- `src/evaluate.py` - full test + corruption evaluation, confusion matrix,
  misclassified grid, reload check.
- `src/prepare_data.py` - parquet -> 32x32 arrays (requires the dataset; not bundled).
- `src/app.py` - FastAPI demo: upload form, `/api/predict` JSON, `/sample?idx=N`
  live prediction on a held-out test image.
- `src/demo_grid.py` - `demo_predictions.png` (24 real test predictions).
- `tests/` - pytest suite (6 tests).
- `final_model.pt` - the trained model the metrics above come from.
- `metrics.json` - full metrics incl. per-epoch validation history.

title: Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision)
text:
Traffic-Sign Recognition on GTSRB (real-world computer vision) - Reproduce
pip install -r requirements.txt
    # download tanganke/gtsrb parquet files into data/, then:
    python3 src/prepare_data.py train && python3 src/prepare_data.py test
    python3 src/prepare_data.py motion_blur
    python3 src/train.py --seconds 100 --max-epochs 24   # repeat until done=true
    python3 src/evaluate.py
    python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
    python3 -m uvicorn app:app --app-dir src --port 8000
